themes.blurb: Force mate with the pieces you have left.

themes.name: Rook endgames
themes.blurb: Lucena, Philidor, Vancura, the active rook.

themes.name: Minor pieces
themes.blurb: Bishops, knights and the pawns they fight over.

themes.name: Queen endgames
themes.blurb: Queen against pawn, queen against rook.

positions.title: Two rooks: the ladder
positions.tip: One rook cuts the king off, the other checks; leapfrog to the edge.

positions.title: King and queen
positions.tip: Keep the queen a knight's move from the king; never take the last square unless it is mate.

positions.title: King and rook
positions.tip: Box the king, take the opposition with your king, then check on the edge. Use a rook waiting move when the kings face each other.

positions.title: Two bishops
positions.tip: The bishops side by side build a wall on neighbouring diagonals; drive the king to a corner, king in support.

positions.title: Bishop and knight
positions.tip: Mate only in the corner of the bishop's colour. Here the king is already there: use the W-manoeuvre of the knight.

positions.title: Opposition: win with the king in front
positions.tip: Take the opposition with your king, then advance the pawn only when the king can no longer be driven back. The pawn behind the king gives you spare tempi.

positions.title: Opposition with a spare tempo
positions.tip: Step to e3 to take the opposition. Whenever the black king matches you, the pawn move e2-e3 or e3-e4 hands the move back.

positions.title: Reach a key square
positions.tip: The key squares of a pawn on e4 are d6, e6, f6. Get the king there before advancing the pawn.

positions.title: Hold the rook pawn
positions.tip: Stay in the corner. The king cannot be driven out without stalemate.

positions.title: The rule of the square
positions.tip: Count the square from the pawn to the queening rank. The king on a3 is outside it: run.

positions.title: Outside passed pawn
positions.tip: Push the a-pawn: the black king must leave the kingside to stop it, and your king eats the pawns it left behind.

positions.title: The breakthrough
positions.tip: b6! axb6 c6! or cxb6 a6!: give two pawns to make one unstoppable.

positions.title: Lucena: build the bridge
positions.tip: Rd1+ pushes the king away, then Rd4: the rook on the fourth rank shelters your king from checks.

positions.title: Philidor: the third-rank defence
positions.tip: Keep your rook on the sixth rank until the pawn arrives there; then check from behind forever.

positions.title: Vancura: rook pawn on the sixth
positions.tip: Your rook attacks the pawn from the side along the sixth rank; if the white king approaches, check it from the side. Keep your king on g7 or h7.

positions.title: Rook against a far-advanced pawn
positions.tip: The rook alone holds: keep it behind the pawn and bring the king.

positions.title: Pigs on the seventh
positions.tip: The open file leads to the seventh rank; the rook feeds on pawns there.

positions.title: Wrong-coloured bishop
positions.tip: The bishop does not control h8. Shuffle in the corner.

positions.title: Knight stops the pawn
positions.tip: The knight blockades the queening square and the king stays close. Never let the knight be driven off b1 while the king is far.

positions.title: Bishop against knight: the knight on the rim
positions.tip: The knight on a2 has no safe square: c1 and c3 are covered by your king, and b4 is defended by the a3 pawn. Keep the cage shut, bring the king to b2 and win it.

positions.title: Opposite-coloured bishops: the fortress
positions.tip: Keep your bishop on the long diagonal that watches the pawn's path and your king in front of the pawn. Never trade the bishop.

positions.title: Queen against a centre pawn on the seventh
positions.tip: Check, force the king in front of the pawn, and use that tempo to bring your king closer. Repeat until the pawn falls.

positions.title: Queen against a bishop pawn: the draw
positions.tip: With a c-pawn the defender has a stalemate trick: on the corner square the king is stalemated. Learn why this is a draw.

positions.title: Queen against rook
positions.tip: Drive the king to the edge; the rook must stay close to its king or be forked. Win it with a check that also attacks the rook.

positions.title: Opposition: the defender's draw
positions.tip: You move first. Stay in front of the pawn and keep facing the white king with one square between: when it steps forward, step forward to meet it.

positions.title: King on the sixth: always wins
positions.tip: With your king on the sixth rank in front of the pawn, the win does not depend on who moves. Step to the side (Kf6 or Kd6), then push.

positions.title: Distant opposition
positions.tip: Lead with the king, not the pawn. Kd2-e3-e4: the pawn stays back as a spare tempo for when the kings face each other.

positions.title: Run to the corner against the rook pawn
positions.tip: Head for a8 or b7. Once your king stands in the corner in front of the rook pawn, no king can drive it out without stalemate.

positions.title: Step into the square
positions.tip: Draw the square of the pawn: a4 to e4 to e8 to a8. One king step (Ke4) brings you inside it; from there you catch the pawn.

positions.title: The protected passed pawn
positions.tip: The black king must watch the protected pair and cannot take it. Your king is free: walk to the kingside and take the g-pawn.

positions.title: Triangulation: lose a move
positions.tip: With Black to move, Black loses. Your king walks a triangle (Kg5, Kf5, Kg6) while the black king can only go back and forth, and the same position returns with Black to move.

positions.title: Two connected pawns
positions.tip: Bring the king up first. Connected pawns protect each other: the black king cannot take the front pawn while the back one guards it.

positions.title: Short-side defence
positions.tip: Your king went to the short side, so your rook checks from the long side, far away (Rd1+, Re1+), where the white king cannot attack it.

positions.title: King cut off by a file
positions.tip: Your rook on the f-file keeps the black king away from the pawn. Advance king and pawn together; when the checks run out, the pawn walks in.

positions.title: The rook belongs behind the passed pawn
positions.tip: A rook behind the pawn gains squares with each push; the black rook in front of it loses them. Push, and bring the king to escort it.

positions.title: Rook against pawn: cut the king off
positions.tip: Cut the king off from the pawn along a file or rank, then bring your king. The pawn falls when the black king cannot defend it.

positions.title: Lucena with Black
positions.tip: Your king is on b1 in front of the pawn. Check the white king away, then put the rook on the fourth rank (Rd4) to block the side checks: the bridge.

positions.title: Rook pawn: the king in the corner
positions.tip: Check the white king from the side. Your king sits in the corner in front of the pawn; an a-pawn is the hardest rook-ending pawn to win with.

positions.title: Rook in front of the rook pawn
positions.tip: The white king is buried on a8. Keep your rook on the a-file or checking from the side, and keep your king on b7 or c7 next to the corner.

positions.title: Rook against knight
positions.tip: Keep the knight next to your king. A knight far from its king is caught or forked by the rook; a knight beside its king holds.

positions.title: Rook against bishop: the safe corner
positions.tip: Your bishop is dark-squared and your king is in the light corner a8: there a check can always be blocked by the bishop. Stay in the corner the bishop does not control.

positions.title: Bishop and the right rook pawn
positions.tip: The bishop is dark-squared and the queening square h8 is dark: the right bishop. Take g7 away with the bishop and the king has nowhere to go.

positions.title: Run to the wrong corner
positions.tip: The bishop is light-squared; h8 is dark. If your king reaches h8, nothing can drive it out. Run.

positions.title: Opposite bishops: two pawns far apart
positions.tip: Two pawns three files apart overload one king and one bishop. Your king supports the g-pawn; the c-pawn ties the black bishop down.

positions.title: Good knight against bad bishop
positions.tip: Black's pawns stand on light squares, the bishop's own colour, so the bishop defends them from behind and attacks nothing. Your knight reaches e5 and wins g6.

positions.title: Knight stops the pawn on the seventh
positions.tip: Nd3+ checks the king and attacks b2 at once: the king must step aside and the knight takes the pawn.

positions.title: Queen against a knight pawn on the seventh
positions.tip: A knight pawn is won like a centre pawn: check until the king stands in front of the pawn, then bring your king one step closer.

positions.title: Queen against a rook pawn, king nearby
positions.tip: A rook pawn draws only when the attacking king is far away. Here your king is close: one check and Kb3 builds a mating net.

positions.title: Queen against rook: Philidor position
positions.tip: The rook must stay next to its king. Use queen checks and a waiting move to hand Black the move: the rook must then step away and is forked.

positions.title: Queen mate with Black
positions.tip: The same method from the other side: keep the queen a knight's move from the king, shrink the box, then bring your king.

positions.title: Rook mate with Black
positions.tip: Cut the king off with the rook, bring your king, and check when the kings face each other.

positions.title: Two bishops: the last moves
positions.tip: The king is already in the corner. Keep it there without stalemate: leave it one square to shuffle on, and mate when your king is close.

positions.title: Queen and rook
positions.tip: Queen and rook need no help from the king: they take turns cutting the king off, rank by rank.

positions.title: Two rooks with Black
positions.tip: The ladder again: one rook cuts, the other checks. Keep the rooks far from the white king.

positions.title: Bishop and knight: the right corner
positions.tip: The bishop is dark-squared and h8 is dark: mate is possible in this corner. Bring the knight to f5 and h6 while the bishop takes g7.

positions.title: Bishop and knight: one step from the corner
positions.tip: Take g7 and f7 away first. The king must go to h8 or h7; then the knight closes the net.
